CamNet · Purchase Orders · Change Summary

Two Purchase Order flow fixes, built and proven in the sandbox

Accounting reported two problems on purchase orders. A Will Call order could not be created without a ship-to address, and a line added to an existing order did not move the order total until the amount was edited and saved twice. Both are fixed. This page shows the before and after inside Flow Builder, and where the change stands.

01

What was asked

Five requirements, drawn from the two reported problems and from the behaviour that had to keep working around them.

RequirementSolution
Create a Will Call purchase order without a ship-to address. Ship To is no longer a required field on the PO Info screen, and the “Ship To is NULL!” error now fires only when Ship To is empty and no Will Call Location was picked.
Keep a pick-up order free of a shipping address, so the vendor is not told to ship an order that will be collected. An order created with a Will Call Location saves with Ship To blank. Nothing later in the flow reads Ship To, so the record simply carries an empty field.
Still stop an order that has neither a ship-to address nor a pick-up location. The error screen is kept. A third condition was added to the existing rule rather than the rule being removed.
A line added to an existing purchase order updates the order total on the first save. A new formula IsNewLine = ISNEW() and a new NewLine outcome send a created line down the same recompute path an edited line already used.
Do not disturb the totals behaviour that already works on an edit. NewLine sits last in the outcome order, after every existing rule. Every existing rule is change-based and cannot match on a create, so none of them is pre-empted.
02

What changed

Both flows keep every version, so the screenshots below are the real prior version opened side by side with the built one, not a reconstruction.

Create Purchase Order, v22 to v23 screen flow

The order-creation screen flow that accounting runs from a Work Order. The shape of the flow did not change. One screen field stopped being mandatory and one decision rule gained a condition.

Before (v22). The prior version, byte-identical to what production runs today. Header reads Create Purchase Order - V22 and Deactivated, because v23 now holds the active slot in the sandbox.

After (v23). The same elements in the same order. No element was added, removed or moved. The change is two settings inside existing elements, shown next.

two conditions, either one enough

Before (v22), the Test Ship To decision, outcome Ship To is NULL. Outlined in red: Any Condition Is Met (OR) over exactly two conditions, both reading PO Info > Ship To > Record ID, one Is Null and one Is Blank. Either one on its own sent the run to the error screen, so an empty Ship To stopped the order no matter what else the user had filled in.

custom logic and a third condition

After (v23), the same outcome, same place on screen. The dropdown now reads Custom Condition Logic Is Met, the logic below it reads (1 OR 2) AND 3, and there are three numbered conditions. 1 and 2 are untouched and both ask whether Ship To is empty. 3 is the new one and asks whether PO Info > Will Call Location Is Blank. Because condition 3 is joined by AND, the error screen is now reached only when Ship To is empty and no Will Call Location was chosen. A Will Call order passes straight through to Test Vendor and Create PO.

The second half of this fix has no Builder control

Ship To also stopped being a mandatory field on the PO Info screen. Flow Builder draws no required checkbox for a lookup component, so opening that field in the screen editor shows the same panel in v22 and v23 and there is nothing to photograph. It is a one-line metadata change, quoted here in full. Without it the screen itself would still refuse to move on with Ship To empty, before the decision above ever ran.

Create_Purchase_Order_Datatable > screens > POInfo > fields > ShipTo
- <isRequired>true</isRequired>
+ <isRequired>false</isRequired>

POLine Sync Quantities to WO Line, v8 to v9 record-triggered flow

The flow that recomputes the purchase order totals whenever a line changes. It runs after save on create and on update. The recompute path existed already. Nothing routed a brand new line into it.

Before (v8). The prior version, byte-identical to production. Same trigger, same elements. The run counters on the canvas are the sandbox history of that version.

After (v9). Identical shape again. The only additions are a formula resource and one more outcome on the EditCriteria decision, neither of which draws a new box on the canvas.

list stops here

Before (v8), the EditCriteria decision. The outcome list outlined in red ends at InvoiceReceived, then falls straight to Default Outcome. A decision runs the first outcome whose conditions match, and every outcome in that list is change-based, so a created line matched none of them and the order total was never rewritten.

new outcome, placed last

After (v9), the same decision. A new outcome NewLine appears in the outlined position, after every existing outcome and before the default. Placing it last means it can never take an update away from an outcome that already handled it. What is inside that outcome is shown next.

What the new path actually does

the only condition on the new path

After (v9), the NewLine outcome selected. It carries exactly one condition, outlined in red: resource IsNewLine, operator Equals, value True. Note the radio below it, If the condition requirements are met. The existing outcomes cannot use that setting, which is what the next two frames explain.

Boolean, ISNEW()

After (v9), the IsNewLine formula resource. Outlined in red: data type Boolean and the formula body ISNEW(). ISNEW() returns true only on the save that creates the record, which is the one moment the old outcomes could never catch. The resource is new in v9 and did not exist in v8.

all three say Is Changed

The reason a created line used to fall through, seen on CostQtyEdited. This is the outcome that already recomputed the totals on an edit. Outlined in red, all three of its conditions use the operator Is Changed, joined by Any Condition Is Met (OR). On a create there is no previous value, so nothing "is changed" and none of the three can be true. The grey note at the bottom of the panel says the same thing from the other side: an Is Changed condition locks the outcome to updates only. Every other pre-existing outcome in this decision is built the same way, which is why a new line reached the default outcome and stopped.

Where the new path goes

already worked
the new path

After (v9), the outcome branches leaving EditCriteria. Outlined in red, CostQtyEdited and NewLine are the only two branches whose connectors keep running down the canvas. Every other branch in view, StatusDelivered, InvoiceReceived and Default Outcome, ends in a red stop marker. The two live connectors run to the same place.

both connectors arrive here

After (v9), the recompute chain. The connector entering from the top right is where those two branches merge, and it lands on GetAllOtherPOLines, outlined in red. From there the existing chain runs unchanged: POLinesLoop3 walks every line on the order, AddToSalesAmount adds each line's extended and net figures, and UpdatePO writes the result back to the order's Sales Amount and Net Total. Nothing in this chain was added or edited. The new outcome simply joins it, so a created line is totalled by the same code that has always totalled an edited one.

The mechanics in one paragraph

On a create, no field "is changed", so the seven pre-existing outcomes cannot fire and the run used to end at the default outcome without touching the order. The new outcome fires only when ISNEW() is true, and it hands off to the same GetAllOtherPOLines → POLinesLoop3 → AddToSalesAmount → UpdatePO chain that already recomputed Sales Amount and Net Total on an edit. That is the whole change. No existing outcome, element or variable was modified, and the flow API version is untouched.

POLine_Update_Create_Sync_Quantities_to_WO_Line: the new formula resource
+ <formulas>
+     <description>TRUE when this PO Line Item was just created, so a brand new line also recomputes the Purchase Order totals.</description>
+     <name>IsNewLine</name>
+     <dataType>Boolean</dataType>
+     <expression>ISNEW()</expression>
+ </formulas>

decisions > EditCriteria: the new outcome, appended after InvoiceReceived
+ <rules>
+     <name>NewLine</name>
+     <conditionLogic>and</conditionLogic>
+     <conditions>
+         <leftValueReference>IsNewLine</leftValueReference>
+         <operator>EqualTo</operator>
+         <rightValue><booleanValue>true</booleanValue></rightValue>
+     </conditions>
+     <connector>
+         <targetReference>GetAllOtherPOLines</targetReference>
+     </connector>
+     <label>NewLine</label>
+ </rules>

Where it stands deploy state

  • Sandbox only. camnet-agentdev carries deploy 0AfO100000dJ7NVKA0. Create Purchase Order is active at v23 and POLine Sync Quantities is active at v9. The metadata was pulled back out of the org afterwards to confirm the active versions really contain the change.
  • Production is untouched. camnetProd still runs v22 and v8. Nothing was deployed, validated or written there. The production deploy waits on your go.
  • Rollback is one action. If the new versions ever need to come out, activate v22 and v8 again from Setup, Flows. The old versions are still in the org and are untouched.
  • The failure case still fails. A run with no Will Call Location and no Ship To was tried on purpose and still stopped on the “Ship To is NULL!” error screen, which is the intended behaviour.
  • No printed or emailed output changed. Neither flow writes a PDF or an email body, so there is no before and after document render to show.

Found while testing, deliberately left alone out of scope

Two pre-existing quirks

Deleting a line leaves the Net Total negative. That happens in a separate delete flow, Purchase_Order_Line_Delete_Update_Sales_Amount, which subtracts the deleted line from zero instead of resumming the lines that remain. It is older than this work and neither flow above can reach it. It needs its own fix.

The order screen wants every selected row edited. If a row is ticked in the line table, its Quantity to Order has to be typed in as well, or the screen refuses to move on. That check is unchanged and was already there.
